userStories.title: Secret routes join gate-secret, and POST reads stop being approvable
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Classify the six exceptions before gating the remaining writes.

**Motivation** — 5a, 5b and 5c-1 gated 62 routes.

**Approach** — **Three routes move to `gate-secret`.** This applies the 5b ruling ("a route whose answer is a token or secret shown once") to `POST /agents` and `POST /agents/:slug/rotate-key`, which answer `apiKey` in clear, and extends it to an input secret: `POST /admin/users` carries `password`, which `ApprovalRequest.input` would store as plain JSON for deciders to read.

**Three POST reads become non-approvable.** `catalog.ts` gains `READ_ACTION_KEYS = new Set(['kb.search', 'context.query', 'retrieval.evaluate'])`. `isReadKey(key)` answers true for a key whose last segment is `read` or that is in this set, so these keys become risk `low` and `approvable: false`, as design §4 says ("Reads are not approvable"). No role changes: the role matrix grants keys, not risks. A policy naming one of these keys is refused by policy validation from then on, as for any non-approvable key.

US-001: `SECRET_GATE_ROUTES` gains `POST /agents`, `POST /agents/:slug/rotate-key` and `POST /admin/users`, and their `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` rows are relabelled `gate-secret`. The rows of `POST /context/:slug/query`, `POST /projects/:slug/kb/search` and `POST /projects/:slug/kb/evaluate/retrieval` are deleted (their keys are no longer approvable, so the contract would report them stale).

**Each gating story removes its own `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` rows**, as in 5c-1. US-001 relaxes the exact gated-route count to a lower bound (at least 62) and the allowlist count case to the `gate-fleet` and `gate-secret` labels; US-013 restores both exactly.

**Scope** — In: catalog predicate/export, local derivation in catalog.spec.ts, secret/read allowlist edits, approvableKeys DTO-key filtering, existing validateApprovalPolicy rejection checks and transitional contract assertions. Out: gating any of the 19 writes (US-002–US-012), removing the core-domain type label and restoring final counts (US-013), and implementing secret gates. Migrating stored approval policies whose pattern names `kb.search`, `context.query` or `retrieval.evaluate`: none ship by default, and the engine no longer consults them. Updating `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-action-inventory.tsv`: the read-key rule is code (`READ_ACTION_KEYS`), not an inventory column.

**Interface** — `READ_ACTION_KEYS = new Set(['kb.search', 'context.query', 'retrieval.evaluate'])`; `isReadKey(key)`; `findCatalogEntry(key)`; `approvableKeys()`; `SECRET_GATE_ROUTES`; `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES`.

Keep all existing permissions/role grants and approval defaults. Change the permission-contract fixture asserting POST /memory as core-domains to POST /admin/users as gate-secret, assert the 11 secret labels, and let the route collector grow from at least 62 until US-013. Test with no DB for catalog/allowlist behavior and real booted-app integration for allowlist equality and zero violations; restore prototype/env mocks and use isolated approval rows.

userStories.title: Gated agent update and capabilities update, and auth-cache eviction after commit
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate both global agent mutations and prevent pre-commit auth-cache eviction on deferred agent writes.

**Motivation** — 5a, 5b and 5c-1 gated 62 routes.

**Approach** — **Auth-cache invalidation waits for the commit.** `AgentsService.update`, `.updateCapabilities` and `.removeById` (5b's deferred `agent.delete` runs it) evict the agent's auth cache (`agentAuthProvider.invalidateByTag`), and `UsersAdminService.update` evicts the user's (`cache.invalidate`), right after their write returns. Inside the execution transaction that is before the commit, so a concurrent request can re-cache the old state for the cache TTL: a disabled user or a deleted agent keeps authenticating. Each now hands the eviction to `AfterCommitService.defer(task)` (exported by the global `PermissionsModule`), and runs it at once when `defer` answers false (no scope open: the immediate path). The approval execution opens the scope (`afterCommit.scope`), so a deferred write's eviction runs after its commit.

This story implements the agent half; US-004 owns the user half.

Route contracts (Scope is projectId passed to ApprovalRouteGate.run):
- `PATCH /agents/:slug` | `agent.update` | null | `rest:agents.update` | `{ slug, patch: parseBody(UpdateAgentDto, …) }` | `agents.update(slug, patch)`.
- `PATCH /agents/:slug/update-capabilities` | `agent.capabilities.update` | null | `rest:agents.update-capabilities` | `{ slug, agentId, capabilities: parseBody(UpdateCapabilitiesDto, …) }` (the DTO of `agents/dto/update-capabilities.dto.ts`; the handler resolves `agentId` with `findBySlug` before gating, as 5b's `agent.delete` does, so a recreated slug is never retargeted) | `agents.updateCapabilities(agentId, capabilities)`.

**Only the HTTP handlers change.** Controller helper methods (`createAgent`, `updateAgent`, `updateAgentCapabilities`, …) and their spec cases stay. Gated handlers keep their parameters, in order; the only handlers that gain a parameter are the three sync handlers (above).

Every body-returning command declares `toResult: (result) => result` unless the row says otherwise; a no-body command declares none. On `executed` the handler answers as today (`JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result)`, or no body for the 204 and empty-200 routes).

**Scope** — In: AgentRouteCommands/AGENT_ROUTE_VARIANTS update and updateCapabilities registrations; both @ApprovalGated handlers with ApprovalPending mapping; defer eviction in update, updateCapabilities and removeById; remove the two pending rows. Out: roster-specific command/self bypass (US-003), user-cache eviction (US-004), and secret agent gates. Moving the other post-write cache evictions of `AgentsService` (`generateApiKey`, `rotateApiKey`, `remove`) after commit: none of them runs inside an execution transaction after this feature.

**Interface** — `AgentsService.update(slug, dto)`; `AgentsService.updateCapabilities(agentId, dto)`; `AgentsService.removeById(id)`; `AfterCommitService.defer(task)`; `AfterCommitService.scope`; `AGENT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.update = 'rest:agents.update'`; `AGENT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.updateCapabilities = 'rest:agents.update-capabilities'`.

Add AfterCommitService after audit and before the two optional AgentsService constructor seams, providing new AfterCommitService() in affected service/create/pickup/audit spec modules. Existing immediate eviction assertions remain. Commands use parseRouteInput for ids/slugs and parseBody with {} fallback for missing body members, then the shared principal loader. Keep @Requires and @ApiResponses. Unit tests cover registrations, frozen immutable-id execution, controller executed/pending mapping and scoped/unscoped cache timing; new HTTP integration tests create unique target agents per AC, grant the acting agent both global keys, seed wait policies, clear approval rows before each test and approve with root.

userStories.title: Gated project-agent update
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate key-holder project-agent writes while preserving unconditional self-update after the roster check.

**Motivation** — 5a, 5b and 5c-1 gated 62 routes.

**Approach** — **An agent's own update is never gated.** `PATCH /projects/:slug/agents/:agentSlug` lets an agent update itself without `agent.update` (graceful OFFLINE shutdown), and a policy on `agent.update` must never make that wait. After the roster check, the handler tests self first: an agent principal whose slug is `agentSlug` calls `agentsService.update` directly, whatever keys it holds, and the handler does not ask `can`. Any other caller is asked `permissions.can(principal, 'agent.update')` (403 `permissions` when denied, as today) and is then gated with `keyCheck: false`, because the handler already proved the key.

**The project-agent update is global.** Its key `agent.update` is a global key, so it gates with `projectId: null`, as today's handler asks the key "without a project context". Its command re-checks the roster when it runs, through `AgentsService.updateRosteredAgent(projectSlug, agentSlug, dto)` (new), which throws `NotFoundAppException({}, 'projectAgents')` when the agent is no longer on the roster and otherwise calls `update(agentSlug, dto)`.

Request checks the handler makes today stay before the gate, so they answer as today and open no request: the roster check and the key-or-self check of `PATCH /projects/:slug/agents/:agentSlug` (404 / 403 `projectAgents`, 403 `permissions`). Every other check (membership, attribution, replace checks, conflicts, dedup) runs inside the command, at once or after approval; a failing check settles the request `failed`. This is 5a's rule.

Route contract: `PATCH /projects/:slug/agents/:agentSlug` (key holders only) | `agent.update` | null, `keyCheck: false` | `rest:project-agents.update` | `{ slug, agentSlug, patch: parseBody(UpdateAgentDto, …) }` | `agents.updateRosteredAgent(slug, agentSlug, patch)`.

**Scope** — In: self-first controller branch after existing roster refusals; new roster-rechecking service method; ProjectRouteCommands registration; pending-row removal. Out: general agent routes/cache implementation (US-002) and project-scoped replacement of the global key.

**Interface** — `AgentsService.updateRosteredAgent(projectSlug, agentSlug, dto)`; `PROJECT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.updateAgent = 'rest:project-agents.update'`; `permissions.can(principal, 'agent.update')`; `ApprovalRouteGate.run({ key: 'agent.update', variant: PROJECT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.updateAgent, projectId: null, input: { slug, agentSlug, patch: updateDto }, keyCheck: false })`.

Retain handler parameter order and all unrostered/self refusal behavior. Commands parse strings with parseRouteInput and patch with parseBody, use identity toResult and rebuilt principal, then reuse the deferred eviction added in US-002. Add AgentsService last to ProjectRouteCommands, updating its spec and approval-execution.service.spec.ts construction. Controller unit tests assert exact gate inputs and that self calls neither can nor gate; service specs cover removed roster. Integration tests use a unique rostered target agent per AC, a globally authorized acting agent and a global wait policy, including target-self with and without the global key. Pending outcomes throw ApprovalPending; executed outcomes keep JsonResponse.Ok.

userStories.title: Gated admin user update and outbox retry
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate global user updates and outbox retries while preserving last-admin protection, JWT-only outbox access and commit-safe user-cache eviction.

**Motivation** — 5a, 5b and 5c-1 gated 62 routes.

**Approach** — **The outbox retry is gated, but agents cannot reach it.** `AdminController` keeps its class-level `JwtAuthGuard`, a passport JWT guard that refuses an agent API key with 401, so only users call these routes and a user always executes at once. The route is gated so the contract has no approvable write route outside the engine, as 5c-1 did for ticket watching. Widening the outbox routes to agents is out of scope.

**Auth-cache invalidation waits for the commit.** `AgentsService.update`, `.updateCapabilities` and `.removeById` (5b's deferred `agent.delete` runs it) evict the agent's auth cache (`agentAuthProvider.invalidateByTag`), and `UsersAdminService.update` evicts the user's (`cache.invalidate`), right after their write returns. Inside the execution transaction that is before the commit, so a concurrent request can re-cache the old state for the cache TTL: a disabled user or a deleted agent keeps authenticating. Each now hands the eviction to `AfterCommitService.defer(task)` (exported by the global `PermissionsModule`), and runs it at once when `defer` answers false (no scope open: the immediate path). The approval execution opens the scope (`afterCommit.scope`), so a deferred write's eviction runs after its commit.

This story implements the user half; US-002 owns the agent half.

Route contracts:
- `PATCH /admin/users/:id` | `user.update` | null | `rest:admin-users.update` | `{ id, patch: parseBody(UpdateUserDto, …) }` | `users.update(principal.id, id, patch)`.
- `POST /admin/outbox/:eventId/retry` | `outbox.retry` | null | `rest:admin-outbox.retry` | `{ eventId }` | `outboxAdmin.retry(eventId)`, answering `null` (no `toResult`).

`AuthRepositoryModule` imports only `PrismaModule`, so no module cycle is added. Each gated handler gains `@ApprovalGated()`, keeps its `@Requires` and `@ApiResponse`s.

**Scope** — In: UserRouteCommands and OutboxRouteCommands, both modules' engine/auth imports, both controllers' gate injection, two pending-row removals, user auth-cache invalidation after outer commit. Out: user creation and its plaintext password/secret gate and agent service changes (US-002). US-004 only: agent access to the outbox admin routes (their class-level `JwtAuthGuard` refuses an API key); the retry route's 202 path is unreachable over REST, and its `openapi.json` operation still lists `202`, as every gated route does.

**Interface** — `USER_ROUTE_VARIANTS.update = 'rest:admin-users.update'`; `OUTBOX_ROUTE_VARIANTS.retry = 'rest:admin-outbox.retry'`; `UsersAdminService.update(actorId, userId, patch)`; `OutboxAdminService.retry(eventId)`; `AfterCommitService.defer(task)`.

Inject AfterCommitService last into UsersAdminService and defer both tag and direct-key auth-state evictions, running immediately and awaited without a scope. Keep the service's self-disable, last-admin locking, token version and audit logic inside the command; domain refusal of an approved update settles failed. New UserRouteCommands uses parseBody(UpdateUserDto, missing patch ?? {}), parseRouteInput and identity toResult; OutboxRouteCommands parses eventId and stores no result. Pending maps to ApprovalPending; update retains JsonResponse.Ok and retry retains an empty 200. Module registration tests are unit-level with GlobalStubsModule (resolve/init UserRouteCommands); new HTTP integration creates fresh users/dead outbox events per AC, grants global keys, uses root decisions, clears approval rows and verifies the unchanged agent 401.

userStories.title: Gated project skill enable and disable, and code-intel index
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate project skill enablement/removal and commit indexing with unchanged results and one indexing audit.

**Motivation** — 5a, 5b and 5c-1 gated 62 routes.

**Approach** — **The code-intel audit callback moves into the command.** `CodeIntelController.indexCommit` passes `astIndexService.indexCommit` an `onIndexed` callback that records the audit entry. The command's run passes the same callback, so the entry is still written once, inside the indexing write.

Route contracts:
- `PUT /projects/:slug/skills/:skillId` | `skill.project.enable` | project | `rest:project-skills.enable` | `{ slug, projectId, skillId }` | `ProjectSkillDto.fromDomain(await skills.enableProjectSkill(projectId, skillId, principal.id))`.
- `DELETE /projects/:slug/skills/:skillId` | `skill.project.disable` | project | `rest:project-skills.disable` | `{ slug, projectId, skillId }` | `skills.disableProjectSkill(projectId, skillId)`, answering `null`.
- `POST /code-intel/index` | `codeintel.index.write` | project (from the body's `projectSlug`) | `rest:code-intel.index` | `{ projectId, index: parseBody(IndexCommitDto, …) }` | `astIndex.indexCommit(index.repoId, index.commitHash, index.files, projectId, <the audit callback>)`.

Every body-returning command declares `toResult: (result) => result` unless the row says otherwise; a no-body command declares none. On `executed` the handler answers as today (`JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result)`, or no body for the 204 and empty-200 routes).

**Scope** — In: new ProjectSkillRouteCommands and CodeIntelRouteCommands; SkillsModule provider; CodeIntelModule engine/auth imports/provider; gate injection into ProjectSkillsController and CodeIntelController; three metadata/gate conversions and pending-row removals. Out: skill source resolution (US-010) and code-intel read handler changes. userStories.title: Gated single-issue and full VCS sync
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate manual issue imports and split GitHub fetches from atomic deferred ticket writes.

**Motivation** — 5a, 5b and 5c-1 gated 62 routes.

**Approach** — **The three sync handlers gain the project.** `VcsController.syncIssue`, `.syncAll` and `.syncPr` have no `@CurrentProject()` today; each appends `@CurrentProject() ctx: ProjectContext` as its last parameter and gates with `projectId: ctx.project.id`. US-008 changes syncIssue/syncAll; US-009 changes syncPr.

`VcsManualSync` takes the project slug (the input carries it; the execution locks that slug to the request's project) and owns what the three sync handlers do today (find the project with `ProjectsService.findBySlug`, which answers the `key` the ticket refs need, check the encryption key, read the connection, build the provider, call `VcsSyncService` / `VcsPrSyncService`, shape the answer). The handlers keep only the encryption-key check, then gate. `syncIssue` still answers 409 (`HttpException('Issue already synced', CONFLICT)`) for an already-synced issue; a deferred one settles `failed`.

`VcsSyncService` gains `syncIssues(project, issues, repo, auditKey, { isolate })`: `fullSync` calls it with `isolate: true` (today's per-issue catch), the deferred callback with `isolate: false` (the first error propagates).

**A deferred sync is all or nothing.** Today `fullSync` and `syncPrStatus` catch each item's failure and continue. Inside the execution transaction that cannot work: a failed nested write poisons the transaction, and the poisoned commit leaves the request `approved` instead of `failed`. The deferred callbacks therefore let the first item failure propagate, so the transaction rolls back and the request settles `failed`. That covers every swallowing site: the per-issue catch of `fullSync`, the per-link catch of `syncPrStatus`, the catch around its 404-close write, and the catch in `handleMergedPrAutoTransition` (which gains a `{ rethrow }` option). Sync all issues — read the connection, fetch and filter all issues; callback — re-read the connection and compare `vcsTestTarget` and `allowedAuthors`, then sync every issue, all or nothing.

**Motivation** — 5a, 5b and 5c-1 gated 62 routes.

If the actor's key is revoked during `prepare`, after the initial execution precheck passed but before the post-prepare key re-check, the import has already happened when the request settles `permission-revoked` (ruled 2026-10-29).
